cells.reason: A real file outside the workspace holding a fresh canary is requested by absolute path, by parent traversal and through a symlink substituted into the sealed tree: every attempt is refused, and neither the in-memory operation evidence nor the durable audit journal, also after a reopen, records a successful read of it. A control read of an inside file proves the detectors see a successful read.

Production route not yet evidenced: the tests below run the prototype sandbox (Landlock, seccomp, private mounts) on the capture host, not the Podman command cell of the guest. The cell is Covered only with a guest-route-bash-view artifact: denied reads of the registered outside-workspace target by absolute path, parent traversal and symlink through bash in the guest command cell, with a control read, bound to the run profile and source. Prototype evidence: A bash cat of a canary file outside the Landlock ruleset, by absolute path and through a symlink in the cell root, exits non-zero with a permission denial and releases no canary byte; an inside control file is read by the same command. The cell is the prototype sandbox (Landlock, seccomp, private mounts) on the capture host, not the podman command cell of the guest.

Production route not yet evidenced: the tests below run the prototype sandbox on the capture host, not the Pi runtime cell of the guest. The cell is Covered only with a guest-route-direct-runtime artifact, produced by tbound-profile guest-evidence route-denied --route direct-runtime from a probe run of the signed cell entrypoint inside the Pi runtime cell (a route-probe cell template: the production template plus a route_probe member; same image, mounts, Landlock ruleset and user mapping): the open and the directory listing of the registered target by absolute path, parent traversal and /proc/self/root are each refused with EACCES or EPERM, the target is shown from outside the cell to exist and be readable by other users, and a control read inside /work succeeds, bound to the run profile and source. The registered target must be a symlink-free canonical path: the permission baseline is measured on its absolute name and the validator refuses any walk that passes a symbolic link on any component (fs.protected_symlinks is not a file permission); the traversal and /proc/self/root names are attempts only and give no baseline. The producer, the entrypoint gate and the validator are tested offline; no in-cell run has been made. Prototype evidence: A process in the cell opens the outside canary file by absolute path, by parent traversal and through a symlink: every open fails with EACCES or EPERM and returns no byte, while an inside file is read in the same probe run.

Classification only; provider-channel confidentiality is outside H1. A proposed read of an outside file is denied by the trusted executor (the result is withheld and the conversation closed) or by the gate (a DENY tool message without output): no provider request carries the canary content. The path the model itself proposed is in the history by design. A control executor that really reads the file puts the canary into the next provider request, so the detector is live.
